disclaimer: DEMONSTRATION CONTENT — illustrative safety checklists written by the ASTRA Health development team (AI-assisted). They are NOT approved NASA flight procedures and contain no medication, treatment or clinical-intervention guidance. Real missions follow procedures approved by the mission medical team.

procedures.title: Routine monitoring
procedures.purpose: Keep continuous monitoring running while all readings are within the demo reference ranges.

steps.text: Keep all sensors attached and powered.
Continue normal activities; no action is required.

procedures.title: Sensor reading check
procedures.purpose: Find out whether an unusual reading comes from the body or from the sensor before acting on it.

steps.text: Stay still for about 30 seconds so the sensor can settle.
Check that the sensor is correctly placed, clean and in firm contact with the skin.
Check the sensor cable or wireless link indicator.
Take a confirmation reading (button below).
If a backup sensor is available, compare its reading.

procedures.title: Sensor artifact — data hygiene
procedures.purpose: The confirmation reading did not reproduce the abnormal values, so the stream is attributed to the sensor.

steps.text: Re-seat or replace the affected sensor.
Confirm that the excluded readings are labelled as sensor artifact in the log.
Send an informational report to Earth so the ground team knows about the sensor event.

procedures.title: Vital-sign deviation — general safety checklist
procedures.purpose: Reduce immediate operational risk and gather information while the situation is assessed by qualified people.

steps.text: Stop the current physical task or exercise session.
Move to a stable, secured position (seat or restraint).
Tell a crewmate and ask them to stay nearby.
Check the habitat environment readouts (cabin pressure, O₂, CO₂) on the vehicle display.
Keep the sensors attached and continue monitoring.
Prepare a structured incident report for Earth (Earth Link module).

procedures.title: Medical support request
procedures.purpose: Bring qualified people into the loop. ASTRA Health does not provide medical advice.

steps.text: Notify the Crew Medical Officer (CMO) on board now.
Send the structured incident report to the ground flight surgeon (subject to signal delay).
Follow only procedures approved by the mission medical team.
Record every action taken; ASTRA Health logs time-stamped entries automatically.
